change.para: the status API now exposes processes, requests, responses, and latency at the top level and for each application. Global statistics cover only currently configured application instances; removing or replacing an application removes its previous statistics from the totals. Connection statistics were removed.
application process statistics include stopping processes separately from running and idle processes, until the router receives a process removal notification.

request statistics expose total, waiting, processing, and completed. Total counts application dispatches, excluding requests rejected before dispatch. Waiting and processing replace active; completed includes errors, cancellations, and WebSocket upgrades.

response statistics count 1xx through 5xx statuses when final headers are prepared for sending, including Worker-generated errors for an application. The 1xx class counts 101 upgrades only. Later body errors do not add a response.

processing latency statistics expose p50, p95, and p99 in milliseconds over a rolling 60-second window. Samples cover ended acknowledged requests and exclude waiting time. Global percentiles use merged application histograms. Short durations use the high-resolution monotonic clock where available.

Go application processes could remain blocked after reaching the configured request limit. Removed ports now close their sockets, and the application library handles end-of-file notifications without retrying indefinitely.
Linux runtime packages include a combined Python/PHP bundle, a checksum-verifying installer, persistent launcher state, and configuration and status commands.

change.para: initial release of Worker, an application server for PHP, Python, Go, and Ruby.
dynamic application configuration through a JSON control API, with process scaling, on-demand process management, and application restarts.

HTTP serving over IPv4, IPv6, and Unix sockets. Applications without targets require one listen address. Python and PHP applications with targets require one listen address per target and no application-level listen. Addresses are unique across all applications and targets; targets share their application's process pool.
listen address updates preserve application processes and in-flight requests. A failed bind leaves the previous configuration active.
request, connection, and application process statistics through the status API.
Linux Python and PHP runtime packages for amd64 and arm64, available as tar.gz archives and deb packages with the language runtime and shared libraries included.
